title: Per-tenant SSE snapshots for interrupted streams and transparent replay
creator: Asha Patel
description: Several enterprise customers reported repeated partial transcripts and unrecoverable SSE disconnects during long-lived generations. Investigation shows a combination of transient edge disconnects, missing last-chunk flushes at the runtime, and lack of a deterministic per-session resume point. This ticket implements per-tenant lightweight session snapshotting at deterministic token boundaries to enable transparent replay/resume across Hosted API, while maintaining compatibility for Dedicated and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Server-side per-tenant session snapshots persisted to durable storage within 200ms of token boundary
Resume API can restore last confirmed token offset and continue generation without duplicate tokens in 99% of tested reconnect scenarios
SDKs (JS/Python) can call resume with no schema change to customer-facing API and preserve streaming ordering
Postfix reassembly tests covering edge disconnect, mid-chunk truncation, multi-chunk reorder in CI with golden transcripts
Canary rollout to 5% of hosted traffic with no >1% increase in latency P95
success_metrics: Reduce customer escalations for SSE truncation by 80% within 30 days of full rollout
Resume success rate (no duplicate or missing tokens) >= 99.5% across synthetic fault injection matrix
No more than 0.5% increase in hosted per-token CPU usage at P50 after snapshotting enabled
notes: Design: take snapshots at final token boundaries (token end markers) to avoid mid-token ambiguity. Snapshots contain opaque session id, confirmed-seq, KV-cache pointer, and minimal model state required for resume. Keep payloads < 1KB per snapshot to bound storage/IO.

Trade-offs: synchronous snapshotting increases write rate; mitigated by coalescing frequent tiny writes into a short-lived in-memory buffer flushed on token boundary and after major events (error/EOF). For Dedicated/Private, snapshot destination is configurable (S3, customer NFS, or local WAL).

Telemetry: add resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_duplicate_token_count, last_token_boundary_latency. Surface these as per-tenant metrics in Console. Add a derived alert for resume_success < 98% for a tenant over 15m.
Compatibility: Resume semantics are backward compatible. If runtime snapshot unavailable, fall back to current behavior (client-visible stream restart) and emit a degraded-compat label in traces.

Rollout plan: implement server + storage + SDK patch behind feature flag. Canary to 5% hosted traffic, validate metrics for 48h, widen to 25%, validate 7d, then full rollout. Dedicated customers can opt-in via config toggle; Private customers will get an upgrade bundle with local snapshot adapter.

Runbook: include playbook steps for 'ghost-chunk' or 'final-chunk-lost' incidents: 1) force resume with newest snapshot, 2) if duplicate tokens observed, instruct SDK to dedupe using transcript checksum guidance, 3) escalate to oncall with session snapshot sample and debug trace IDs.
Open questions: retention window for per-tenant snapshots (default 12h vs 72h), and encryption-at-rest approach for Private deployments (customer-managed KMS required?).
